description: MediaMTX server (MIT license) integration library for VisioForge SDKs
releaseNotes:
* [ALL] Changed: the DirectShow filter and SDK installers, the Delphi and ActiveX All-in-One installers, the macOS package and the Unity package now send the same short install report as the Windows .NET SDK installer: the outcome, the product, its version and whether it was a first install or an upgrade. Turn it off with `INSTALLREPORT=0` for a Windows installer, the file `/Users/Shared/VisioForge/no-install-report` on macOS, or `VISIOFORGE_INSTALLREPORT=0` for Unity. The redist installers and NuGet packages send nothing.
* [Android] Fixed: the hardware HEVC encoder listed High tier levels for codecs that support only Main tier, so the stream caps it reported did not match what the codec wrote.
* [Core] Fixed: `MediaInfoReaderX.GetFileSnapshotRGB`, `GetFileSnapshotSKBitmap` and `GetFileSnapshotBitmap` with a position past the end of the file now return no frame at once instead of after the whole timeout.
* [Demos] Added: `ARM64 Player Demo`, a Media Blocks SDK .NET WinForms file player built as a native Windows on Arm app, with a readme on the ARM64 packaging traps.
* [Demos] Added: six console samples from the video shorts - `extract-frames-short-console`, `cut-video-short-console`, `udp-mpegts-short-console`, `audio-capture-short-console`, `hls-webcam-short-console` and `pre-event-short-console`.
* [Media Blocks SDK .NET] [Media Player SDK .NET] [Video Capture SDK .NET] [Video Edit SDK .NET] Added: `VideoRendererSettingsX.KeepLastFrame` (and `VideoRendererBlock.KeepLastFrame`) keeps the last frame on the view after the end of the media and after Stop instead of clearing it, on every view and platform of the X engines and Media Blocks; while stopped, `VideoRendererBlock.Snapshot_Get` returns that frame. The default is `false`, as before.
* [Media Blocks SDK .NET] Changed: with `AudioEnabled` off, `RTSPSourceBlock` has no `AudioOutput` (`null`) and `RTSPSourceSettings.IsAudioAvailable()` returns `false`; a pipeline that connected that output used to never start.
* [Media Blocks SDK .NET] Changed: `FallbackSwitchSourceBlock.GetStatistics()` could crash the application with an access violation, most often after the main source restarted; its values are now plain numbers instead of `GLib.Value` objects, and `GetStatus()` returns the state by name (`Stopped`, `Buffering`, `Retrying`, `Running`) instead of a number.
* [Media Blocks SDK .NET] [Video Capture SDK .NET] Fixed: on Windows, `DeviceEnumerator.VideoSourcesAsync()` could return no cameras, or leave one out now and then, mostly in virtual machines with USB passthrough; the cameras are now listed, and when none can be, a warning names the cause.
* [Media Blocks SDK .NET] [Media Player SDK .NET] [Video Capture SDK .NET] Fixed: an H.264 or H.265 RTSP source that joined a camera stream between key frames showed and recorded grey or black pictures until the next key frame; it now starts with the first key frame and asks the camera for one on start.
* [Media Blocks SDK .NET] [Media Player SDK .NET] [Core] Fixed: several `Position_SetAsync` calls in a row (`MediaBlocksPipeline`, `MediaPlayerCoreX`, `SimplePlayerCoreX`, and `MediaPlayerCore.Position_Set_TimeAsync`), such as a dragged seek bar, could leave playback at an earlier position; the last one requested now always wins.
* [Media Blocks SDK .NET] Fixed: `VideoRendererBlock.Snapshot_Get` returned `null` on a WPF `VideoView` and with `autovideosink` (the native view on Linux); it now returns the frame on screen.
* [Media Blocks SDK .NET] [Video Edit SDK .NET] Fixed: the HEVC `Profile` of the NVENC, Quick Sync, Media Foundation and VA-API encoder settings was ignored by `VideoEditCoreX` (always Main), and `HEVCEncoderBlock` with `Main10` or `Main444` failed to start; the requested profile is now written, and a profile the encoder cannot produce fails the start. A 10-bit source with the default Main profile is now written as 8-bit; set `Profile = Main10` to keep 10 bits.
* [Media Blocks SDK .NET] [Video Edit SDK .NET] Fixed: `VAAPIH264EncoderSettings.Profile` was ignored (always High); it now applies, and its default is `High`, so output that never set it stays the same.
* [Media Player SDK .NET] Added: `MediaPlayerCore` with `Source_Mode = Memory_DS` and `MediaInfoReader.GetStreamAvailabilityFromMemoryStream` work without LAV Filters installed, including streams that cannot seek (played start to end).
* [Media Player SDK .NET] Changed: Blu-ray playback (`MediaPlayerSourceMode.BluRay`) and `MediaInfoReader.ReadBluRayInfo` no longer use LAV Filters: they play the largest `.m2ts` of the disc with the FFMPEG Source and need the `VisioForge.DotNet.Core.Redist.FFMPEG` package. ISO images, playlist files, multi-clip titles, menus and encrypted discs are no longer supported and fail with `OnError` naming the reason.
* [Media Player SDK .NET] Fixed: encrypted file playback (`Encrypted_File_DS`) could crash the application, most often with `Audio_Channel_Mapper`, and failed with "Unable to create corresponding decryptor" in a NuGet-only install; both work now.
* [Media Player SDK .NET] Fixed: `Multiple_Video_Streams_Mappings_Add` could not play an AVI with several video streams ("Video stream 0 not found").
* [Media Player SDK .NET] Fixed: with `ConsoleUsage = true`, a failure mid-stream raised no `OnError` and moved to the next playlist file, closing the renderer window left `Play()` waiting forever, and `Loop` was ignored; all three now behave as without `ConsoleUsage`.
* [Video Capture SDK .NET] Fixed: `VideoCaptureCoreX.StartAsync` never returned for an RTSP or ONVIF camera with audio opened with `audioEnabled: false` while `Audio_Play` was on (the default); a regression of 2026.11.20.
* [Video Capture SDK .NET] Fixed: `VideoCaptureCore` Desktop Duplication screen capture kept recording the old area after `Screen_Capture_UpdateParameters` moved it while nothing on the screen changed.
* [Video Capture SDK .NET] [Media Player SDK .NET] [Video Edit SDK .NET] Added: in native Windows ARM64 apps, the video effects and frame events, picture-in-picture, audio mixing and enhancement, the WASAPI audio renderer and Desktop Duplication screen capture now work (`VisioForge.DotNet.Core.Redist.Base.arm64`).
* [Video Capture SDK .NET] [Media Player SDK .NET] [Video Edit SDK .NET] Fixed: DirectShow filters could fail to load - with "Unable to load filter module" (0x7F) on a computer that also has an older VisioForge product installed, and (0x7E) from a custom redist folder added with `CustomRedist.AddPath`; the SDK now loads its own redist libraries in both cases.
* [Video Capture SDK .NET] [Media Player SDK .NET] [Video Edit SDK .NET] Fixed: `Audio_Channel_Mapper` mapping a multichannel source to fewer channels, such as 5.1 to stereo, played no audio ("Unable to connect audio renderer").
* [Video Capture SDK .NET] [Media Player SDK .NET] [Video Edit SDK .NET] Fixed: the FFMPEG Source could crash the application or play distorted sound when the audio changed its channels mid-stream, such as AC-3 going from 5.1 to stereo.
* [Video Capture SDK .NET] [Media Player SDK .NET] [Video Edit SDK .NET] Fixed: encryption with a missing key (`MP4Output.Encryption`, `FastEncrypt_Start`, playback of an encrypted file) now fails with an error naming the missing key, a wrong key fails playback with an error, and a key that does not match `Encryption_KeyType` is refused; before, `FastEncrypt_Start` showed a password window and wrote an empty file, and a `byte[]` key with the default key type encrypted with the password "System.Byte[]".
* [Video Edit SDK .NET] Changed: `VideoEditCore.Start()` with `ConsoleUsage = true` and `Mode = Preview` now raises `OnError` and returns `false`; a console app has no view for the preview.
* [Video Edit SDK .NET] Fixed: `VideoEditCore` could not open a video with more than two audio channels, such as an MP4 with 5.1 AC-3, without LAV Filters; such audio is now mixed down to stereo.
* [Video Edit SDK .NET] Fixed: the `VideoEditCore` preview of a timeline with audio froze after repeated seeking, and `Position_Get` and `StopAsync` no longer returned.
* [Video Edit SDK .NET] Fixed: `VideoEditCore` reported a conversion that failed mid-stream as successful and wrote tags into the truncated file; it now raises `OnError` and stops with `Successful = false`.
* [Video Edit SDK .NET] Fixed: `VideoEditCoreX` ignored the H.264 `Profile` and `Level` of the encoder settings (`OpenH264EncoderSettings` with `High` produced Constrained Baseline); the profile now applies for every encoder and the level for OpenH264, and `SmartRender` re-encodes a segment whose profile does not match.
* [Windows] Added: the FFMPEG Source DirectShow module holds two more filters, VisioForge FFMPEG Video Decoder (MJPEG, H.264, HEVC, MPEG-2, MPEG-4, VC-1, with hardware decoding) and VisioForge FFMPEG Audio Decoder (MPEG audio, AAC, AC-3, E-AC-3, DTS, TrueHD, Vorbis, PCM). The SDKs do not use them yet.
* [Windows] Added: the FFMPEG Encoder DirectShow filter takes FFmpeg encoder options per input pin through `IFFmpegSinkPinSettings2` (any encoder option by name, video decimation, an FFmpeg audio filter graph), and writes Speex in Ogg and native FLAC files.
* [Windows] Added: the VLC Source DirectShow filter has a native ARM64 build (`visioforge_vlc_source_sdk_setup_arm64.exe`) with libVLC 3.0.24.
* [Windows] Changed: the standalone FFMPEG Source DirectShow filter setup installs the current module with FFmpeg 9, registers both filters and rolls back if it cannot, no longer adds its folders to `PATH`, and needs 64-bit Windows.
* [Windows] Changed: the VLC Source DirectShow filter setups no longer set `VLC_PLUGIN_PATH` or add their `Redist` folder to `PATH` (upgrading removes both), and the x64 setup writes its registry key to the 64-bit view.
* [Windows] Fixed: the FFMPEG Source DirectShow filter dropped video frames - about half of an AVI with H.264 B-frames, and the first frame of a file with repeated decode times (WMV3 in MKV) - and swapped red and blue in top-down RGB24 output; the FFMPEG Video Decoder started AVI video 40-80 ms after the audio.
* [Windows] Fixed: an MP4 or MOV file written by the FFMPEG Encoder DirectShow filter lost its last video frame: the file ended where that frame starts. The last frame now keeps its duration, with every encoder.
* [Windows] Fixed: without a set sample rate, the FFMPEG Encoder DirectShow filter could pick an output rate far from the source's, and MP2 at a bit rate the source rate does not take failed to start; it now picks the nearest rate that works.
* [Windows] Fixed: with Smart App Control turned on, Windows blocked the DirectShow filters and DLLs installed by the SDK, redist, Encoding Filters Pack, FFMPEG Source, Video Encryption SDK and Video Encryptor installers; every binary they install is now code-signed.
* [Windows] Fixed: the VLC Source DirectShow filter setups: the first open after installing took about 40 seconds (the plugin cache now ships), a failed registration reported success, uninstalling left the filter registered or unregistered another copy of it, the setups removed an installed Virtual Camera SDK, and their Start-menu links went into the wrong folder.
* [Windows] Fixed: the x86 and x64 VLC redist setups removed each other and installed into the other bitness's folder; both now install side by side.
* [Windows] Fixed: uninstalling a .NET redist left its folder, `PATH` entry and registry key behind; uninstalling the SDK left its filters' security catalog installed (one more copy per upgrade) and re-registered its LAV filters instead of unregistering them; cancelling the SDK installer sent no report.
